findings.title: kickReserveAuction can be called while a bad-debt liquidation is still unsettled, draining reserves and shifting the loss to HPB depositors
findings.evidence: kickReserveAuction() (src/base/Pool.sol:419) immediately calls KickerActions.kickReserveAuction (line 421) without checking that pending liquidations are settled; unlike repayDebt/addQuoteToken/moveQuoteToken (lines 158, 194, 229) it never invokes the available _revertIfAuctionClearable guard (src/libraries/helpers/RevertsHelper.sol:50). For a borrower whose auction already lost all collateral but still has t0Debt (borrower.t0Debt != 0 && borrower.collateral == 0), settle() has not yet removed that unrecoverable bad debt, yet poolBalances.t0Debt still includes it. KickerActions.kickReserveAuction computes the claimable amount via _claimableReserves(t0PoolDebt, ...) (src/libraries/helpers/PoolHelper.sol:299), where claimable = 0.995*debt + balance - (buffer*deposits + bonds + unclaimed); the unrecoverable debt therefore inflates the reserve auction. Any external user can call kickReserveAuction() and then takeReserves() to sell/claim those reserves while the liquidation is unsettled (permissionless, nonReentrant only). Once the reserves are transferred out, settle()'s step 2 ('settle debt with pool reserves', SettlerActions.sol:132-146) finds assets <= liabilities, so it cannot absorb the bad debt, and step 3 _forgiveBadDebt (SettlerActions.sol:457) removes the loss from the next HPB buckets' deposits, imposing it on HPB depositors instead of pool reserves. The upstream fix added _revertIfAuctionClearable (commit 656eccf7, testReserveAuctionUnsettledLiquidation) and later the stricter _revertIfActiveAuctions (commit e258a849, 'Liquidation of positions with bad debt can cause losses for HPB depositors') at exactly this entry point.
